ssdim.py.summary: Group similar files by their ssdeep fuzzy hashes.
details: Hashes every file below the current directory with ssdeep, clusters the files whose compare score exceeds the threshold and can copy or move each cluster into a ``groupNNN`` directory, writing a CSV/JSON report of the similarity matrix.

ssdiper.py.summary: Find the similar files of a directory with five different similarity hashes.
details: ``--alg`` selects tlsh (default), ssdeep, sdhash, simhash or minhash; the hashes are computed for every file, compared pairwise and stored in ``simz.json``, and ``--group-similar`` moves the related files into ``group001``, ``group002``... folders.

ssdiper2.py.summary: Group similar files by ssdeep hash with minified function names.
details: Computes the ssdeep digests, keeps the pairs above the similarity threshold in ``simz.json`` and optionally moves each related cluster into a ``groupNNN`` subdirectory (``-g``). The internal helpers carry single-letter names from an earlier size-optimisation pass.

ssize.py.summary: List the entries of the current directory with their sizes.
details: Measures each entry (directories recursively, symlinks skipped), prints them ascending by size with the human-readable value and closes with the total.

strip_html_tags.py.summary: Extract the plain text of HTML files.
details: Parses the markup with :mod:`html.parser`, drops the scripts, styles and head content, turns the block-level tags into line breaks and writes the extracted text back or to the chosen output, processing whole trees in parallel.

strip_installed_pkgs.py.summary: Remove the already-installed packages and the stdlib names from a requirements file.
details: Normalises the requirement names, drops the ones that are installed or part of the standard library, sorts the result and rewrites the file in place, printing how many entries were removed.

striper.py.summary: Strip the leading and trailing whitespace of every line of a file.
details: Rewrites the file with each line stripped on both sides, printing ``<file> cleaned.`` or the error when the file is missing.

striptags.py.summary: Strip selected tags and attributes from HTML with BeautifulSoup.
details: A click CLI that removes the tags by bundle (``hs`` for the headings, ``metadata``, ``structure`` ...) or by name, can keep only the ``href``/``alt``/``meta`` attributes, drops the hidden elements and rewrites the document with normalised whitespace.

stripy.py.summary: Strip the docstrings from Python files with libcst.
details: Removes the module, class and function docstrings (optionally only the short ones), collapses the emptied bodies to ``pass``, keeps the formatting of the rest of the code intact and processes the tree in a worker pool with a per-file report.

subdir.py.summary: Extract archives into a subdirectory named after the archive.
details: Detects zip, tar and 7z archives, creates a sibling directory with the archive's stem and unpacks the members into it, guarding against path traversal.

summar.py.summary: Summarise a text file with TextRank and save the summary next to it.
details: Runs ``summa``'s summarizer at a 70 % ratio, writes the result to ``<name>_summsry.txt`` and prints it.
summar.py.notes: The entry point refers to ``syd.argv`` instead of ``sys.argv``, so running the script directly raises ``NameError`` until that typo is fixed; use :func:`summarize_with_summa` programmatically.

svg2png.py.summary: Convert an SVG file to PNG with CairoSVG.
details: Writes the ``.png`` next to the source and, with ``-r``, deletes the original SVG.

symlink_so.py.summary: Create the ``.so.0``/``.so.1`` symlinks of the libraries in ``~/.local/lib``.
details: Skips the files that are already symlinks or carry a version suffix, derives the ``libfoo.so`` base name, repairs the wrong links and points ``libfoo.so.0`` and ``libfoo.so.1`` at it, which is what the loaders of the Termux builds expect.

system_pkgs_reinstaller.py.summary: Reinstall a list of apt packages with resumable progress.
details: Reads the package names, keeps the completed ones in a ``.progress`` JSON file so an interrupted run can continue, clears the cached ``.deb`` files after each install and retries the ``apt install --reinstall`` failures.
